intro: You are at Urfa Castle in Şanlıurfa province, a citadel of the 9th century looking down on the pool of Balıklıgöl. Look for its two Corinthian columns, and the Syriac inscription between them: they are left from a monument raised by the kings of Edessa.
history: Since the kingdom of Edessa, this citadel above the pool of Balıklıgöl has been the city's defence, and it took its present form in the ninth century. At its eastern end stand two Corinthian columns, with a Syriac inscription between them — survivors of a monument raised by king Manu of Edessa. Locally, they have another name: the throne of Nimrod.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the twin columns and the Syriac inscription, then the rock-cut ditch and the curtain walls.
facts: Did you know? The northern ditch was cut into the living rock, turning the citadel into an island against any attack from the hill. And the two Corinthian columns at its eastern end survive from a monument raised by king Manu of Edessa; locally they are called the throne of Nimrod.
outro: This brings our journey through Urfa Castle to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These columns have stood for centuries; let them keep standing for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
